## Commands (in this order)

Run top to bottom. Lines marked `# VERIFY` need a human check first. Optional backups are commented out.

```bash

# --- 1. Route 53 records pointing at deleted or doomed targets
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z1 --change-batch '{"Changes":[{"Action":"DELETE","ResourceRecordSet":{"AliasTarget":{"DNSName":"dualstack.gone-lb-999.us-east-1.elb.amazonaws.com.","EvaluateTargetHealth":false,"HostedZoneId":"Z35SXDOTRQ7X7K"},"Name":"api.example.com.","Type":"A"}}],"Comment":"sweeper teardown"}'
# VERIFY: points at legacy-clb-1.us-east-1.elb.amazonaws.com, which this plan tears down: delete the record first
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z1 --change-batch '{"Changes":[{"Action":"DELETE","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"legacy.example.com.","ResourceRecords":[{"Value":"legacy-clb-1.us-east-1.elb.amazonaws.com"}],"TTL":60,"Type":"CNAME"}}],"Comment":"sweeper teardown"}'
# VERIFY: points at legacy-prod.us-east-1.elasticbeanstalk.com, which this plan tears down: delete the record first
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z1 --change-batch '{"Changes":[{"Action":"DELETE","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"old.example.com.","ResourceRecords":[{"Value":"legacy-prod.us-east-1.elasticbeanstalk.com"}],"TTL":300,"Type":"CNAME"}}],"Comment":"sweeper teardown"}'

# --- 2. ECS services at 0 desired
aws ecs delete-service --cluster arn:aws:ecs:us-east-1:123456789012:cluster/c1 --service zero --region us-east-1

# --- 3. Elastic Beanstalk environments
aws elasticbeanstalk terminate-environment --environment-id e-old --region us-east-1

# --- 4. Elastic Beanstalk applications
aws elasticbeanstalk delete-application --application-name legacy --region us-east-1

# --- 5. Load balancers with no healthy targets
aws elbv2 delete-load-balancer --load-balancer-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:us-east-1:123456789012:loadbalancer/app/old-lb/1111111111111111 --region us-east-1

# --- 6. Classic load balancers with no healthy instances
aws elb delete-load-balancer --load-balancer-name legacy-clb --region us-east-1

# --- 7. Target groups with zero registered targets
aws elbv2 delete-target-group --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:us-east-1:123456789012:targetgroup/empty-tg/cccccccccccccccc --region us-east-1

# --- 8. NAT gateways with no traffic since the cutover
aws ec2 delete-nat-gateway --nat-gateway-id nat-idle --region us-east-1
aws ec2 release-address --allocation-id eipalloc-nat --region us-east-1

# --- 9. EC2 instances stopped since before the cutover
# VERIFY: t3.large stopped since 2026-08-01; vol-data survive termination (DeleteOnTermination is off): delete them after
# backup: aws ec2 create-image --instance-id i-stopped --name pre-teardown-i-stopped --no-reboot --region us-east-1
aws ec2 terminate-instances --instance-ids i-stopped --region us-east-1

# --- 10. RDS instances stopped or with no connections since the cutover
# VERIFY: no connections since the cutover (peak DatabaseConnections 0); deletion protection is on: turn it off with modify-db-instance first
aws rds delete-db-instance --db-instance-identifier legacy-db --final-db-snapshot-identifier legacy-db-final-20261027 --region us-east-1
# VERIFY: stopped; AWS starts a stopped instance again after 7 days, and compute bills again
aws rds delete-db-instance --db-instance-identifier stopped-db --final-db-snapshot-identifier stopped-db-final-20261027 --region us-east-1

# --- 11. RDS manual snapshots taken before the cutover
# VERIFY: manual snapshot of deleted-db, which no longer exists: it may be the last copy of that database (keep one, or export it to S3 first)
aws rds delete-db-snapshot --db-snapshot-identifier orphan-final --region us-east-1
aws rds delete-db-snapshot --db-snapshot-identifier pre-migration --region us-east-1

# --- 12. AMIs not used by any instance
# VERIFY: AMI created before the cutover and not used by any running or stopped instance
aws ec2 deregister-image --image-id ami-old --region us-east-1

# --- 13. EBS snapshots
aws ec2 delete-snapshot --snapshot-id snap-ami --region us-east-1
# VERIFY: snapshot taken before the cutover; managed by AWS Backup or Data Lifecycle Manager: change the plan/policy instead
aws ec2 delete-snapshot --snapshot-id snap-backup --region us-east-1
aws ec2 delete-snapshot --snapshot-id snap-old --region us-east-1

# --- 14. Unattached EBS volumes
# backup: aws ec2 create-snapshot --volume-id vol-old --description 'pre-teardown copy of vol-old' --region us-east-1
aws ec2 delete-volume --volume-id vol-old --region us-east-1

# --- 15. Unassociated Elastic IPs
aws ec2 release-address --allocation-id eipalloc-free --region us-east-1

# --- 16. Log groups with no events since the cutover
aws logs delete-log-group --log-group-name /aws/elasticbeanstalk/legacy-prod/var/log/web.stdout.log --region us-east-1
```

## Notes

- 1 Aurora cluster member\(s\) in us-east-1 were not checked \(clusters are not covered yet\).
- 1 Route 53 record\(s\) point at load balancers or Beanstalk environments in regions that were not scanned; pass those regions with --region to check them.
- A/AAAA records with plain IPs were not checked; pass --ip-ranges ip-ranges.json \(https://ip-ranges.amazonaws.com/ip-ranges.json\) to flag IPs in AWS EC2 space that this account no longer owns.
